brief.subject: Diesel jumps 7.6 cents to $6.352; cargo theft hits California
brief.headline: Diesel climbs 7.6 cents as Fed holds rates and LTL tonnage turns positive
brief.dek: Diesel rises to $6.352, the Fed holds steady amid inflation, California cargo theft arrests, and Old Dominion sees tonnage growth.
brief.lede: Diesel rose 7.6 cents last week to a $6.352 national average, squeezing margins for carriers without strong fuel surcharge coverage.

sections.heading: Diesel Pops 7.6 Cents
bullets: $6.352 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-10-26.
Up 7.6 cents (1.2%) week over week, so recheck fuel surcharges on spot loads now.
Down 3.0 cents over four weeks, meaning last week's jump erased part of a recent dip.

sections.heading: Fed Holds as Inflation Speeds Up
bullets: Rates unchanged: the Fed kept its main interest rate steady despite accelerating inflation.
Two FOMC members dissented, favoring a 0.25 percentage point hike, so borrowing costs could still rise.
Truck loans and equipment financing stay pricey for small fleets weighing purchases.

sections.heading: California Cargo Theft Crackdown
bullets: $500,000 SIG Sauer shipment left a Torrance warehouse via a fictitious pickup; two people were arrested.
Fake pickups remain a live threat, so verify carrier identity before loading or accepting brokered freight.
Nine alleged Sinaloa Cartel associates were arrested in Southern California over a cargo train theft ring.

sections.heading: Freight Demand Signals Mixed
bullets: Old Dominion posted positive September tonnage, its first growth in more than two years.
OD executives say a full recovery needs broader demand, which depends on easing energy costs.
XPO beat Q3 expectations on higher volumes and stronger pricing, hinting at firmer LTL rates.
CPKC set records for grain and intermodal volumes, adding rail competition for some truck freight.

sections.heading: Claims Worries Hit Brokers
bullets: C.H. Robinson and Landstar shares fell despite strong results, as investors focused on rising claims.
Expect brokers to tighten scrutiny of carrier safety and claims history when tendering loads.
